name: Benidorm
note: British archetype, but half the high-rises are full of Spaniards from Madrid.

name: Magaluf
note: Stag and hen capital. Germans are three miles east and never meet them.

name: Platja de Palma
note: Ballermann. The German Magaluf, down to the beer steins and schlager.

name: Palmanova
note: Magaluf's quieter neighbour. Only just.

name: Alcúdia
note: Family end of the market, tilting German. Old town worth the detour.

name: Cala d'Or
note: Whitewashed calas, German package trade, very quiet by ten.

name: Sant Antoni de Portmany
note: The West End strip. Sunset Strip is the tolerable half.

name: Ibiza Town
note: The one genuinely pan-European crowd on this map.

name: Ciutadella
note: Menorca stayed low-rise and mostly Spanish and British.

name: Torremolinos
note: Where the package holiday was invented. Faded, cheerful, still busy.

name: Benalmádena
note: Arroyo de la Miel and the marina. Bars showing the football.

name: Fuengirola
note: Long beach, long-standing British and Finnish contingents.

name: Marbella
note: Money rather than lager, but Puerto Banús is Puerto Banús.

name: Estepona
note: The Costa del Sol town that kept its old quarter.

name: Nerja
note: Prettier, older crowd. Long-settled British population.

name: Almuñécar
note: Granada's beach. Almost entirely domestic, and all the better for it.

name: Torrevieja
note: Expat belt and Madrid's second home in equal measure.

name: Calp
note: German and Dutch lean. The Peñón is the actual draw.

name: Xàbia
note: Expat belt. Pleasant, and thoroughly colonised.

name: Gandia
note: Valencia and Madrid decamp here in August. Barely a foreign accent.

name: Peñíscola
note: Castle on a rock, packed with Spanish families and Aragonese plates.

name: Benicàssim
note: Domestic beach town that borrows a British crowd for festival week.

name: La Manga
note: A sandbar of flats between two seas. Overwhelmingly Spanish.

name: Roquetas de Mar
note: Big German package presence beside a very Spanish resort town.

name: Mojácar
note: White hill village above a strip of British-leaning beach bars.

name: Lloret de Mar
note: French and Dutch coaches as much as British stag parties.

name: Empuriabrava
note: Canal-side marina town, an hour from the border. Effectively French.

name: Roses
note: The French weekend. Signs and menus follow suit.

name: L'Escala
note: Anchovies, Greek ruins at Empúries, and a French summer crowd.

name: Cadaqués
note: Dalí's village. French day-trippers and Barcelona money.

name: Salou
note: PortAventura feeder town. British, French and Spanish families all.

name: Cambrils
note: Salou's grown-up neighbour: seafood, and a domestic crowd.

name: Sitges
note: Barcelona's beach and a long-standing gay resort. Cosmopolitan.

name: Barcelona
note: Everyone. The French arrive by train in numbers nobody counts.

name: San Sebastián
note: Twenty minutes from France, and it shows all summer.

name: Hondarribia
note: Border town. Half the terrace is over from Hendaye for lunch.

name: Zarautz
note: Surf beach with a Spanish and French crowd, no package trade.

name: Santander
note: Where Madrid goes to escape August. Sardinero is all domestic.

name: Llanes
note: Green coast, cider, and Spanish families who booked last October.

name: Gijón
note: A working city with a beach, and almost no foreign tourism.

name: Sanxenxo
note: Galicia's summer capital. Madrid and Galicia, nobody else.

name: A Coruña
note: Glass balconies, good food, and a domestic crowd.

name: Conil de la Frontera
note: Seville and Madrid in August. Atlantic wind keeps the package trade off.

name: Zahara de los Atunes
note: Tuna, dunes, and a well-heeled Spanish crowd.

name: Chiclana
note: Novo Sancti Petri is where German package holidays go on the Atlantic.

name: Tarifa
note: Kitesurfing brings the Germans; the wind keeps everyone else away.

name: El Puerto de Santa María
note: Sherry, tuna and a Sevillano summer crowd.

name: Gibraltar
note: Not a resort, actually British. Marks and Spencer and monkeys.

name: Granada
note: The Alhambra draws every nationality on this map at once.

name: Jaca
note: Ski and mountain town. Spanish, with French over the pass.

name: Albufeira
note: The Strip. Portugal's answer to Benidorm.

name: Praia da Rocha
note: Portimão's beach strip. Cliffs are genuinely good, crowd is not.

name: Lagos
note: Backpackers and surfers alongside the package crowd.

name: Vilamoura
note: Golf and marina. Sedate, moneyed, entirely inauthentic.

name: Valencia
note: City break boom: Fallas, paella and a growing British stag trade.

name: Madrid
note: Everyone passes through. August belongs to whoever stayed behind.

name: Bilbao
note: The Guggenheim, and the French over for the weekend.

name: Málaga
note: The Costa del Sol's city, and lately the reason people skip the resorts.

name: Porto
note: Port lodges and cheap flights. As busy as Valencia, on half the residents.

name: Lisbon
note: Tuk-tuks in Alfama. The city that ran out of long lets.

name: Santiago de Compostela
note: Pilgrims of every nationality, and Spanish ones in the greatest number.

name: Seville
note: French city breaks in spring, everyone else in the shade by July.
